name: Giovanni Ferrero
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Giovanni Ferrero is executive chairman of his family's namesake confections business, which boasts $20 billion in annual sales.
The firm is best known for its iconic Nutella chocolate-hazelnut spread, Kinder chocolates and Tic Tac mints.
Giovanni served as co-CEO with his brother, Pietro, who died of a heart attack in 2011.
In 2017 he stepped down as CEO but stayed on as executive chairman to focus on corporate strategy.
Ferrero acquired Nestle's entire U.S. confections business in 2018 for $2.8 billion.
In 2025 it acquired WK Kellogg, the makers behind Corn Flakes and Rice Krispies, for $3.1 billion.
forbes_facts: Ferrero is a novelist who has published eight books.

name: John Fredriksen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Fredriksen's empire includes oil tankers, dry bulkers, LNG carriers and deepwater drilling rigs.
He first got into oil trading in the 1960s in Beirut, bought his first tankers in the 1970s, and ran crude for Iran in the 1980s.
His offshore drilling rig firm Seadrill emerged from bankruptcy in 2018, with Fredriksen helping to raise about $1 billion in new debt and equity.
He also owns a stake in Mowi, which has rolled up competitors to become the biggest fish farmer in the world.
Though set to hand control to twins Kathrine and Cecilie, he has said "My daughters should not have to live with the work everyday I've had."
forbes_facts: Fredriksen gave up his Norwegian citizenship in favor of tax-haven Cyprus.
Fredriksen operates out of a 30,000 square foot mansion in London and relaxes in Marbella.

name: David Steward
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2022)
forbes_bio: David Steward is the founder and chairman of IT provider World Wide Technology.
Steward grew up in the segregated South with seven siblings; his father worked as a mechanic, janitor and trash collector.
After graduating from Central Missouri University, he worked in sales for the Missouri Pacific Railroad, Union Pacific and FedEx before cofounding World Wide Technology in 1990.
In the early days, Steward sometimes went without a paycheck and once watched his car get repossessed from the office parking lot.
Today, he is the majority owner of the $20 billion (sales) company, whose customers include Citi, Verizon and the federal government.
Steward donated $1.3 million to the University of Missouri-St. Louis in 2018 to create the David and Thelma Steward Institute for Jazz Studies.
forbes_facts: Steward's daughter was a producer of the 2016 movie Manchester by the Sea.
Steward's son is the CEO of Polarity and Lion Forge, companies that produces comics, animation and other kinds of entertainment featuring diverse characters.

name: Ron Baron
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Ron Baron is the CEO of Baron Funds, a money management firm he founded in 1982; it manages about $53 billion.
The buy-and-hold investor's flagship fund, Baron Growth, has an annual turnover of less than 1.5% and net assets of about $4 billion.
Baron owns one of the biggest estates in the Hamptons, which he assembled from 2001 to 2009 at a total cost of $152 million. It's worth much more now.
The son of an engineer (dad) and purchasing agent (mom) for the federal government, Baron wanted to be a doctor but didn't get into medical school.
Baron became a securities analyst in 1970 and named his dog Big Mac after one of his first successful stock recommendations.
forbes_facts: To help pay for college, Baron worked as a cabana boy, lifeguard, water-ski instructor and ice cream truck driver.
John F. Kennedy's rocking chair and Babe Ruth's 1920 Yankees contract are two pieces of memorabilia in Baron's Manhattan office.

name: Laurent Dassault
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Laurent Dassault is an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune, which he inherited along with his siblings when her father Serge Dassault died in 2018.
In 1991 after 13 years in banking, Serge joined Dassault Groupe, the family's aerospace and software conglomerate. He is now honorary chairman of the supervisory board.
He also served as a director of Artcurial, the family's art auction house, which auctions horses and real estate
Marcel, Laurent's grandfather, founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
He and his family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
forbes_facts: Dassault is the President of One Drop France, Guy Laliberte's charity, which aims to improve access to clean water
Besides his passion for art, Dassault is an avid polo and golf player.

name: Paul Tudor Jones II
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones II is known for his macro trades, particularly his bets on interest rates and currencies.
In 1980, he founded Tudor Investment Corporation, which now manages some $17 billion in assets.
Jones got his start at his dad's small business paper, the Memphis Daily News, where he wrote under the name Paul Eagle in high school and college.
He cut his teeth trading cotton futures at the New York Cotton Exchange, under the tutelage of renowned cotton trader Eli Tullis.
In 1988, he cofounded the Robin Hood Foundation, with the goal of reducing poverty in New York City.
forbes_facts: Jones, who was a boxing champion in college, took up the sport after he failed to score a single point in sixth grade basketball.
In 2013 he cofounded Just Capital, a nonprofit research outfit that ranks Russell 1000 companies based on their impact on the environment, communities, and more.

name: You Xiaoping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: You Xiaoping is the chairman of Huafon Group, a maker of polyurethane products.
Huafon Group is also involved in metals, finance, logistics and trade.
One of its units, Shenzhen-listed Huafon Chemical, is among the world's largest spandex fiber makers by production volume.

name: Chen Bang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Bang is the chairman of Aier Eye Hospital Group, China's largest ophthalmology chain by the number of outlets.
The company has opened over 900 eye hospitals and centers in China, the U.S., Europe and Southeast Asia.
Aier is headquartered in Changsha in central China's Hunan province.
Chen dabbled in property and overseas investments until meeting a retired ophthalmologist, who inspired him to open his own hospitals.

name: Wang Xin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2007-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Xin is chairman and CEO of Guandong Dtech Technology, which designs and manufactures industrial machinery.
Wang worked as an accountant for a local PCB manufacturer in Guandong before starting her entrepreneurial business.
She took the company public in Shenzhen in 2022.
Wang's husband, Lin Xia, and her brothers, Wang Xue Feng and Wang Feng, are active in the business.

name: Stewart Rahr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Stewart Rahr expanded Kinray, a pharmaceutical distributor his father founded in 1944, and sold it to Cardinal Health in 2010 for $1.3 billion.
Rahr is known for his extravagant lifestyle, which he funds through conservative investments in private equity, hedge funds and natural resources.
After getting a bachelor's degree in history at NYU, he briefly attended NYU Law before dropping out to run the family business.
He has a sizable art collection that includes works by Picasso, Damien Hirst, Jeff Koons and Alexander Calder.
He has donated over $25 million to Make-A-Wish, a nation-wide nonprofit that grants the wishes of critically ill children.
forbes_facts: Rahr calls himself "Stewie Rah Rah No. 1 King of All Fun."

name: Andrew Karam
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Andrew Karam is a cofounder of AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin, which went public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
AppLovin generated $5.5 billion of revenue in 2025.
Karam is one of eight billionaires produced by AppLovin, including cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi.
Karam owned 4% of AppLovin as of September 2024, when he dropped below the SEC's disclosure threshold.
He left the company three months later to focus on philanthropy and investing.
